observations.detail: The full title, 'The relation between simple harmonic motion and circular motion', is readable on two lines in the whole-page image. The English chapter/page breadcrumb and the complete prose column are legible. Paragraphs are left-aligned without first-line indentation; line wrapping, sentence spacing and paragraph gaps do not collide with the figures or captions. The focused viewport also shows readable initial projection prose.

Vector arrows over OA, its magnitude bars, O_1X, omega with subscript zero, phi, t=0, x_m, phi=omega_0 t, and the complete cosine displacement equation are visibly typeset, not raw dollar-delimited TeX. Formula baselines and over-arrows have adequate clearance. No replacement boxes, missing symbols or visibly broken mathematical glyphs were observed. Static parsing of the bound desktop HTML records 20 KaTeX expressions and zero katex-error nodes; this supplements the pixel inspection rather than replacing it.

Two thin horizontal rules are actually visible. The first separates 'The ball itself continues around the circle; it does not move back and forth along that axis.' from 'We can make this projection visible as a shadow.' The second is below Figure 10 and its caption, before 'Hang a weight from a spring where the same parallel light can reach it.' Its preceding prose ends 'We observe its projection, not a new straight-line motion of the ball itself.' Both match the lesson's before/after boundaries. The HTML implements them as bordered p elements with class 'para section', not hr elements.

The standalone conclusion, 'The spring weight and the shadow of the uniformly rotating ball follow the same displacement law.', is visibly bold across two unclipped lines. It is distinct from the surrounding normal-weight explanatory prose and precedes the clarification that the disk does not drive the spring. The bound HTML contains the matching strong element.

Each figure has its own readable, centered numbered caption beneath it with clear separation from adjacent prose. These are the translations of the numbered caption blocks in the bound lesson. No descriptive caption is required or invented: the source-derived caption blocks contain only the figure numbers.

The circle, radius vector, angular arrow, radius-length annotation, dotted centerline/projection guides and separate vertical projection axis are all visible. No label obscures another label, and the meaningful curves, arrowheads and axis endpoints remain inside the displayed figure.

Parallel light arrows, the ball on the disk, the radius and rotation arrow, the screen plane, the shadow, the vertical axis and the displacement arrows are clear. The disk outline, screen edges and lower label leaders are complete; no clipping or illegible text overlap was observed.
